clue.text: Check, one related to ear that's messy

parts.note: CH is the chess notation for check
otic is the anatomical adjective for things of the ear

explanation.surface: Someone checks a person with an ear problem whose situation is untidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in chaos is disordered and untidy, so messy is a plain synonym.

clue.text: 'It's played in confidence' — Les Taylor

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the name, and the start of the surname

explanation.surface: A quoted remark, attributed to one Les Taylor, about something done in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a saying; the whole of 'It's played' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A celesta is a keyboard instrument with metal bars, so it is something that is played.

clue.text: Unit involved in some unspecified periodic payment

indicators.note: in puts the mixed letters inside the next word's equivalent

parts.note: any means some, without saying which

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A company division mixed up in some vague regular payout.
explanation.definitionFit: An annuity is a fixed sum paid out every year, a regular instalment of income.

clue.text: Article on empty space unit

indicators.note: an empty word has its inside cleared out, leaving just the ends

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: A news article about a unit of measurement for a vacuum in space.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a measure of heat energy, used in billing for gas, so it is a unit.

clue.text: Officer deceives board

parts.note: board in the sense of a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A policeman misleads a company's directors.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is the lowest rank of police officer in Britain.

clue.text: Lay out clues with a solver's tip

indicators.note: letters that are out are knocked out of their places and rearranged
the tip of a word is its very end, so only the closing letter is kept

explanation.surface: An instruction to set out the clues, plus a hint for whoever is solving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like a verb meaning set out, but it is the adjective meaning not of the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay people are those outside the clergy, so lay means non-religious or worldly, as secular does.

clue.text: Vicious drugs parties?

parts.note: Sid Vicious, the Sex Pistols bassist
E is ecstasy, so drugs are Es

explanation.surface: Nasty drug-fuelled parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parties' suggests raves, but it means the opposing sides in a dispute; the question mark flags that twist.
explanation.definitionFit: The parties to a dispute or contest are its opposing sides, the teams on each side.

clue.text: Convicted felons with connections

parts.note: surface reading: criminals who know people in high places
setter's reading: the prisoners are literally linked to one another by metal links while they labour

explanation.walkthrough: 'Connections' suggests useful contacts; here it is the physical fetters joining a group of convicts.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain gang is a group of prisoners shackled together while doing outdoor work.

clue.text: Ambassador: he commonly is a beneficiary

parts.note: a legate is an envoy, especially of the Pope
dropping the h, as in casual speech, he becomes 'e

explanation.surface: An envoy, it is commonly said, is someone who gains from a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is someone left a legacy in a will, so a beneficiary of it.

clue.text: Toothy thing's liberal chatter

indicators.note: liberal means free and loose, so the letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: A grinning politician's endless talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet is a toothed bar or wheel with a pawl, so it is a mechanism full of teeth.

clue.text: Light, so aren't moving in line regularly?

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the other pair
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: first and third letters of line

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark about lights that won't move into a regular line.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp, a source of illumination, so it is a kind of light.

clue.text: Current game's unfinished

indicators.note: a word left unfinished loses its final letter

parts.note: the board game also known as checkers

explanation.surface: A match currently in progress has not yet been completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as 'present', but it is the noun: a current of air. Draughts is the British name for checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is a flow of cold air through a room, which is an air current.

clue.text: Spam is 'the works' for the rest of the crew

indicators.note: works suggests being worked over, processed into something new

explanation.surface: A ship's cook declaring that tinned meat is the full feast for the other sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The works' looks like an idiom meaning everything, but 'the' belongs to the letters being mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipmates are fellow sailors aboard the same vessel, i.e. everyone else serving alongside you.

clue.text: Kidnap missing leader? Certainly

indicators.note: without its leader a word loses its opening letter

parts.note: to snatch someone is to abduct them

explanation.surface: A question about an abduction whose ringleader is absent, answered with confident agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Natch is informal slang shortened from naturally, used to mean of course.

clue.text: Anglo-Saxon hairy creature one's neglected until now

indicators.note: the numeral one, as a letter, is left out of the word

explanation.surface: An ancient Englishman's shaggy beast, ignored to this day.
explanation.definitionFit: As yet is an adverbial phrase meaning so far, up to the present time.

clue.text: Ben's motto translated as 'That'll be over my dead body!'

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so the letters are recast

explanation.surface: A man called Ben's defiant motto, rendered as a refusal he will hold to the death.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase is read literally: the thing that ends up lying over a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravestone is laid or set up over a buried body, so it literally sits over the dead.

clue.text: City in which a pair takes daily exercise initially

indicators.note: takes means holds inside, so the pair encloses what follows

parts.note: a pair is slang for a woman's breasts
a daily or char is a cleaning lady

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A city where couples go for their morning workout.
explanation.walkthrough: BUST holds CHAR plus E. A daily is British for a cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names Romania's capital, so it is an example of the broad category given.

clue.text: Rigid Tom needs a boost

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A stiff, tense man named Tom needs a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: A catatonic person is fixed in a stupor, motionless and stiff as a board.

clue.text: Lying about copper (crooked) raking in millions

indicators.note: raking in means gathering something inside

explanation.surface: A corrupt policeman lies about money while making millions.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer, but it is the metal; 'crooked' then reads as BENT, with M inside CU-BENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent describes a person lying down or reclining, the same sense as lying.

clue.text: 'Get back to your old state!' gives Republican a way out

explanation.surface: A command to return home allows a Republican politician to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old state' hints at a US state, fitting Republican; it means a former condition.
explanation.definitionFit: To regress is to revert to an earlier, often less developed condition, so the command says do that.

clue.text: Cask-maker's craft: weaving rope in modest surroundings

indicators.note: in places the mixed letters within the shy word
surroundings means the outer word wraps around the mixed letters
weaving twists strands together, so these letters are intertwined anew

explanation.surface: A barrel-maker weaving rope in humble surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooper makes barrels, and coopery is that trade, so it names the cask-maker's skill.

clue.text: Brummie goes on record over animated artificial human

indicators.note: turned over, the combined letters run the other way

parts.note: the setter refers to himself by his pseudonym
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: The setter goes on record about a robot-like creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Brummie is this puzzle's setter, so his name stands for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish folklore a golem is a clay figure brought to life, a man-made being.

clue.text: Art arranged in row for convenience

indicators.note: in places the reordered letters within the word for a row
arranged means put into a different order

explanation.surface: Pictures hung in a row to make things easier.
explanation.walkthrough: A convenience is the British euphemism for a public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A latrine is a basic toilet, and a public convenience is a polite term for a lavatory.

clue.text: Game that Greece would like to see making a return?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the children's game played with small glass balls

definitions.text: that Greece would like to see making a return?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Parthenon sculptures held in the British Museum, which Greece wants given back

explanation.walkthrough: The Elgin sculptures were taken from the Parthenon to London in the 1800s; Greece has long asked for them back.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the toy spheres and the Parthenon carvings, known as the Elgin collection, go by this plural name.

clue.text: Sheen appearing at last on Casualty?

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: a casualty is a loss, as in battle

explanation.surface: Martin Sheen finally making a guest appearance on the TV hospital drama Casualty.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheen looks like the actor's name and Casualty the BBC medical drama; both are ordinary words here.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloss is a shiny surface lustre, the same as a sheen.

clue.text: One who belittles journalist reversing vehicle

indicators.note: reversing makes the short word for the journalist go backwards

explanation.surface: A critic watches a reporter backing up a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A detractor disparages or runs down others, which is what someone who belittles does.

clue.text: Painter's daughter turned up a shade of green

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: An artist's daughter appeared in a greenish outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was the French Impressionist famous for ballet dancers, an example of an artist.

clue.text: It quivers, similar to a swan

parts.note: a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: Something trembles, like a nervous swan.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen tree is known for leaves that tremble in the slightest breeze, hence quaking aspen.

clue.text: Say, Loren's excited to go inside soon!

indicators.note: the mixed letters are placed within the abbreviation for say
excited letters are agitated and jump about

explanation.surface: Sophia Loren is thrilled at the prospect of going inside shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ere long is an archaic phrase meaning before long, in a short while.

clue.text: Union-related joke about 'turning tail'

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the joke word runs backwards

parts.note: a pun is a play on words

indicators.note: turning shuffles the letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A trade union quip about running away in fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' sounds like a trade union, but it means marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptial is the adjective for a wedding or marriage, which is a union of two people.

clue.text: Reserve cast put by lake

explanation.surface: Stores of throwing tackle kept beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Reserve looks like a stockpile, but it is reticence of manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve as a personal quality means restraint and reticence, which is shyness.

clue.text: Admit high speed force used in breaking noses

parts.note: c is the speed of light, the highest speed

indicators.note: breaking smashes the word so its letters re-form

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to using great force at speed in a nose-breaking assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess is to acknowledge guilt, which is to admit something.
